'''Aharon Kapitulnik''' ([[Hebrew language|Hebrew]]: אהרון קפיטולניק; born 1953) is an Israeli-American experimental [[condensed matter physics|condensed matter physicist]] working at [[Stanford University]]. He is known primarily for his work on strongly correlated electron systems, low dimensional electronic systems, unconventional superconductors, topological superconductors, superconductivity and magnetism, transport in bad metals and precision measurements.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=k89RzXQAAAAJ&hl=en |title=Aharon Kapitulnik }}</ref>

==Education and career==

Kapitulnik studied physics at [[Tel Aviv University]] in Israel (BA 1978, PhD 1983). After completing his doctoral studies under supervision of [[Guy Deutscher (physicist)|Guy Deutscher]] on the physics of disorder he moved to [[United States]] to work on polymers as a postdoc scholar in the group of [[Alan Heeger]] at [[UC Santa Barbara]]. In 1985 he joined the faculty of the Department of Applied Physics of [[Stanford University]] where he became a Professor Applied Physics and Physics in 1994.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://stanford.edu/~aharonk/briefCV2.pdf |title=CV |publisher=stanford.edu}}</ref>

At Stanford, Kapitulnik formed a close collaboration with [[Theodore Geballe]] and [[Malcolm Beasley]] known collectively as the "KGB group".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/physics/laureates/1998/laughlin-bio.html | title=R. B. Laughlin Nobel autobiography | publisher=nobelprize.org}}</ref> Many of its graduates went on to establish successful academic careers in US and around the world.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://web.stanford.edu/group/kgb/old_website/alumni/AlumniDir.html |title=KGB group alumni (incomplete)}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://kapitulnik.stanford.edu/people |title=Kapitulnik group alumni}}</ref>

==Awards==
Kapitulnik is the Theodore and Sydney Rosenberg Professor in Applied Physics at Stanford University<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/aharon-kapitulnik |title=Theodore and Sydney Rosenberg Professor |publisher=stanford.edu}}</ref> and the Sackler Professor by Special Appointment at Tel Aviv University.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://physics.tau.ac.il/sackler_professors |title=Sackler Professorship |publisher=tau.ac.il |access-date=2018-03-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180301230924/https://physics.tau.ac.il/sackler_professors |archive-date=2018-03-01 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He is a Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]], a Fellow of [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]. He was awarded the 2015 [[Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Prize]] of the American Physical Society for the "discovery and pioneering investigations of the superconductor-insulator transition, a paradigm for [[quantum phase transition]]s"<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Kapitulnik&first_nm=Aharon&year=2015|title=O. E. Buckley Prize |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref> and 2009 [[Kamerlingh Onnes Prize|Heike Kamerlingh-Onnes Prize]] for "seminal studies of time-reversal-symmetry breaking effects in unconventional superconductors using magneto optics".<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.m2s-2015.ch/kamerlingh-onnes-prize.php |title=Kamerlingh-Onnes Prize |publisher=2015-International Conference on Materials and Mechanisms of Superconductivity. |access-date=2018-03-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181010210840/http://www.m2s-2015.ch/kamerlingh-onnes-prize.php |archive-date=2018-10-10 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
